findings.where: Screen 3 (At 7.5 bar), the bench and screen 2's Pressure slider
findings.what: The answer 16 mA can be read before Check: the ideal line crosses the 7.5 bar gridline exactly on the labelled 16 mA gridline, and screen 2's slider shows "16.00 mA" at 7.5 bar one tap back. Ask for a pressure that sits on neither grid, such as 6.25 bar (answer 14 mA, slips 10 mA for 62.5% of 16 and 12.5 mA for 62.5% of 20).

"So 5 bar sends 12 mA" gives the result without the step that screen 3 tests next, and the rule of 4 mA plus 1.6 mA a bar appears only in the grey caption. Add one sentence: "Each bar adds 1.6 mA to the 4 mA at the bottom, so 5 bar sends 4 + 8 = 12 mA."

"They are precise but not accurate" uses two terms that no screen teaches, and a steps lesson shows only the frame, so the explain text that defines them never reaches Dan. Write "They agree closely with each other, but all sit 2% high", or teach the pair on screen 10.

The film shows only five beads dropping onto the ideal line with both screws at 0, so the screen's point, slide against tilt, waits for Dan's finger. Let it ease the zero screw up and back, then tilt the span to the still's −0.48 mA, before handing over the sliders.

At 360 px a 0.32 mA zero error lifts the line about 3 px, and a full ±0.80 mA screw moves it only about 8 px, so the table shows the slide and tilt better than the line does. A "gap from ideal, % of span" close-up under the bench, like screen 10's panels, would show a zero error as a flat offset and a span error as a slope.
The Display reads "10.20 bar" and nothing says it is the reading at the 10 bar check point, so the reader cannot tell what pressure is applied. Label it in the picture.
"Errors are counted in per cent of span" reads as true of every instrument, but screen 12 and real data sheets also use per cent of reading. Write "Here, errors are counted in per cent of span".
Screen 8 names and highlights "span error", but "zero error" first appears inside screen 7's Why and is never highlighted on a SHOW screen. Name it on screen 6 or in screen 7's task.

findings.where: Screens 1, 11 and 13, the Why? button on pick puzzles
findings.what: Why? works before any answer, and screen 1's Why names the zero screw, so the opening predict-then-play puzzle can be read off before Dan tries. Hide Why? on pick steps until the first Check, as the typed steps already do.
The display's staircase is drawn in teal, which is kept for small labels. Draw it in ink, as the brief's colour rule asks for a second trace.

findings.where: Screens 10 and 11, panels A and C
findings.what: At 360 px the beads at 0 bar sit on the y axis and crowd its "0" tick label. Nudge the first point right or move the label.

The brief promised the data-sheet words accuracy and repeatability, and a quick recall of Statistics lesson 2's offset against scatter, but no screen names either word. So Dan meets "accurate to ±0.5%" on screen 12 and scatter on screen 10 without the words he will read on every data sheet.

findings.where: Whole lesson (the practice text's best point)
findings.what: Two field lessons never reach a screen: a zero error and a span error can cancel in the middle, so a single mid-range check passes a bad transmitter, and the order is zero, then span, then zero again. One puzzle built from the practice's 0 to 16 bar example would carry both.
The right choice is the longest and the only one that gives a reason, which gives it away. Make the three choices closer in length.

findings.where: Screen 2 and the closing line, for the course as a whole
findings.what: The chain ends at a display, but lessons 5 to 8 all depend on this same number reaching a controller or a trip. Name the controller in the last block, or move the explain text's sentence about an oil pressure trip into the closing line. That sets up measure, compare, act for the rest of the course.
At laptop width single-line choices sit centred, but at 360 px they are left-aligned. Align the button content to the start so both widths match.
